# synthcheck

**Experimental.** synthcheck checks how authentic synthetic survey
respondents are: Whether respondents generated by large language models
resemble the real people they are meant to stand in for.

It looks at three things:

- **Overlap:** Do synthetic respondents land where real people land?
- **Structure:** Do the items relate to each other as they do in real
  people?
- **Behaviour (coming next):** Do synthetic respondents answer the way
  people do, including variability, extreme and midpoint answers,
  acquiescence, consistency and person fit?

Each index will be anchored between a shuffled baseline (0) and a second
sample of real people (100). The **synthetic authenticity benchmark**
compares several models in one table, scored by their weakest column by
default.

The package compares models and supports decisions about them. It does
not show that synthetic respondents can replace a field test.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/synthcheck")
```

## Example

``` r

library(synthcheck)

# Honesty-Humility, Canada: real people and four language models
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
rev_items <- intersect(h, hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$reverse])
keyed <- function(d) { d <- d[h]; d[rev_items] <- 8 - d[rev_items]; d }

real <- keyed(hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ])
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 4, ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model, drop = TRUE),
                    function(m) lapply(split(m, m$attempt), keyed))

cov <- synthetic_coverage(synthetic, real, cor = "pearson")
cov
gg_coverage(cov)
```

## Data

`hexaco_real` holds 17,874 real respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items
from Canada, Great Britain and the United States (Open-Source
Psychometrics Project). `hexaco_llm` holds 59,611 synthetic respondents
from four open-weight language models (10 attempts per country), and
`hexaco_items` holds the item text, facets and keys.

## Related

synthcheck grew out of the coverage strip in
[mirtverse](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/). See the article
[Checking synthetic respondents: The coverage
strip](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/synthetic-coverage.html).

# Package index

## Overlap and Structure

Where synthetic respondents land and how their items relate.

- [`synthetic_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_coverage.md)
  : How well do synthetic respondents cover the real population?
- [`gg_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_coverage.md)
  : Draw the coverage strip
- [`blend_llms()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/blend_llms.md)
  : Find the best blend of language models

## Data

- [`hexaco_real`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_real.md)
  : HEXACO responses of real people, for checking synthetic respondents
- [`hexaco_llm`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_llm.md)
  : HEXACO responses generated by four language models
- [`hexaco_items`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_items.md)
  : The 240 IPIP-HEXACO items and their keys

## Helpers

- [`theme_synthcheck()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/theme_synthcheck.md)
  : A clean ggplot2 theme for synthcheck graphics
- [`synthcheck`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthcheck-package.md)
  [`synthcheck-package`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthcheck-package.md)
  : synthcheck: Check how authentic synthetic survey respondents are
